item.title: The Great Orbital Economy: Who will own the Sky?
item.description: The private space industry is entering a multi-trillion-dollar era. Experts now forecast the space economy reaching on the order of $1 to 2 trillion by 2035. item.title: In the Age of Intelligence, Power Is the New Oil
item.description: Every AI model starts with a dataset and ends with a power bill. As large models and cloud services multiply, the demand for compute has exploded, putting a spotlight on electricity and infrastructure. Bain & Company reports that AI’s compute needs are growing at twice the pace of Moore’s Law, driving global compute demand toward 200 gigawatts by 2030. item.title: Starcloud and the Race to Build the Orbital Cloud
item.description: Space has always been a proving ground for ambition. But what happens when that ambition turns toward the cloud itself? item.title: Mapping the Frontier Stack: Deep-Tech Sectors Shaping 2025 and Beyond
item.description: At a glance, venture capital might seem to be in its own world: hyping trends, chasing valuations, and minting unicorns. But beneath the hype, something interesting is happening: deep tech is quietly growing. While the noise of SaaS rounds and chatbots dominates the headlines, a new layer of venture activity is emerging at the intersection of space, defense, data, AI, and energy.These sectors are no longer isolated verticals, they’re merging into something more integrated, complex, and critical.

item.title: Rocket Lab’s Neutron: A Newcomer Reshaping the Launch Landscape
item.description: Rocket Lab has never tried to be the loudest company in space, but it may become one of the most strategically important. Neutron represents a bold pivot for Rocket Lab, a company known for the small Electron rocket. item.title: The Year AI Moves Into Reality
item.description: For the last two years, artificial intelligence has lived mostly in language. We trained models to talk, reason, summarize, and persuade.
